captions.instagram:
How is curd made?

A spoon of old curd turns a pot of warm milk solid by morning, and nothing was added but bacteria. Zoom into milk, watch them turn milk sugar into acid, see the proteins link up at pH 4.6, then set your own dahi on a winter night and find out why it needs a blanket.

→ A glass of milk is about 87% water. The rest is fat, protein, milk sugar and minerals.
→ Zoom in 100,000 times: protein balls called casein micelles, kept apart by their charged, hairy coats.
→ A spoon of old curd carries living bacteria. In warm milk they double about every half hour, eating milk sugar and making lactic acid.
→ The acid cancels the charge on the micelles. Near pH 4.6 they stick together and build a network.
→ That network is a sponge. It traps the water and fat, and liquid milk becomes a soft solid: curd.

Play with it yourself. It's free and open source: glassbox.how/curdclear (link in bio)

youtubeLong.title: How is curd made? (interactive explainer)
youtubeLong.description:
A spoon of old curd turns a pot of warm milk solid by morning, and nothing was added but bacteria. Zoom into milk, watch them turn milk sugar into acid, see the proteins link up at pH 4.6, then set your own dahi on a winter night and find out why it needs a blanket.

▶ Play with the interactive version: https://glassbox.how/e/curdclear/
⌘ Source code (MIT): https://github.com/bdeeps/curdclear

In this video:
• Milk is water with things floating in it. Cow milk is about 87% water.
• A spoon of jaman is a spoon of bacteria. Old curd carries around a hundred million live lactic acid bacteria in every gram.
• At pH 4.6 the milk sets. The acid pulls the pH down from about 6.7.
• Warmth and time decide the pot. Lukewarm milk at about 40 °C sets in roughly five to seven hours.
• Whey and sourness have causes. The greenish water on curd is whey, squeezed out as the protein network tightens.
• One trick, many foods. Yoghurt is curd made with two named bacteria at about 42 °C.
